entries.name: Strength
entries: While wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with the strength property, your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} is reduced by 10 unless your Strength score meets or exceeds the strength number.

entries.name: Auto
entries: Weapons with the auto property can only fire in burst, penetrating, or rapid modes. If the weapon has any combination of burst, penetrating, and rapid modes, you choose which mode to use. You can only use one mode at a time.

entries.name: Bulky
entries: While wearing armor with the bulky property, you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|sw5e-phb}) checks that rely on sound.

entries.name: Burst
entries: When you would make a ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} with a weapon with the burst property, you can instead spray a 10-foot-cube area within range with shots, consuming ammunition equal to the burst number. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your bonus to attacks with the weapon) or take the weapon's normal damage. Before you use the burst property, you can declare one creature that would be affected by it. If the creature fails its save, in addition to the weapon's normal damage, it is subjected to any additional effects that would occur on a hit. If the targeted area is beyond normal range but within long range, affected targets have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the save.

entries.name: Dexterity
entries: A weapon with the dexterity property requires more skill to control. While wielding it, you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} unless you meet the Dexterity requirement.

entries.name: Disguised
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Charisma ({@skill Deception|sw5e-phb}) checks made to hide the nature of a weapon with the disguised property.

entries.name: Double
entries: A weapon with the double property can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property—the damage when the weapon is used with Double-Weapon Fighting. See the rules for Double-Weapon Fighting in chapter 9.

entries.name: Finesse
entries: When making an attack with a weapon with {@itemProperty SWF|sw5e-phb|the finesse property}, you use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

entries.name: Fixed
entries: A weapon with the fixed property does not fill the hand, but you can't use the weapon while the hand is full. Additionally, you have a +10 bonus to {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks} and {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} to avoid being disarmed of this weapon.

entries.name: Heavy
entries: When you hit with an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} using Strength with a weapon with the heavy property, you deal additional damage equal to half your Strength modifier (rounded up, minimum of +1).

entries.name: Hidden
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|sw5e-phb}) checks made to {@optfeature Conceal|sw5e-phb|conceal} a weapon with the hidden property.

entries.name: Interlocking
entries: While wielding a weapon with the interlocking property, you can use your object interaction to detach the weapon into two separate weapons or reattach into a single weapon. While separated, each weapon has the same damage, damage type, combined value and weight, and properties (except for the double property) as the single weapon.

entries.name: Light
entries: A weapon with the light property is small and easy to handle, making it ideal for use when engaging in Double- or Two-Weapon Fighting. See the rules for Double- and Two-Weapon Fighting in chapter 9.

entries.name: Luminous
entries: A weapon with the luminous property sheds dim light in a 5-foot radius while activated. Additionally, Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|sw5e-phb}) checks made while the weapon is activated have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}.

entries.name: Modal
entries: A weapon with the modal property can switch between modes. A list of weapons in parentheses appears with the property-the weapons between which an exotic weapon can be switched by using an object interaction.

entries.name: Obtrusive
entries: While wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with the obtrusive property, you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|sw5e-phb}) checks that rely on sight.

entries.name: Penetrating
entries: When you would make a ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} with a weapon with the penetrating property, you can instead attempt to penetrate and hit a creature behind the target, consuming ammunition equal to the penetrating number. Make an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} against the initial target. If the attack hits, there is a creature within 15 feet of that creature and directly behind it, and the original {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} would hit the second creature, it also takes normal weapon damage.

entries.name: {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb|Power Cell}
entries: Weapons with the {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb} property are fueled by {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb|power cells}, which must be loaded in order to fire the weapon.

entries.name: Rapid
entries: When you would make a ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} with a weapon with the rapid property, you can instead unload on a single target, consuming ammunition equal to the rapid number. The target must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your bonus to attacks with the weapon). On a failed save, roll the weapon's damage dice twice and add them together, adding relevant modifiers as normal and subjecting the target to any additional effects that would occur on a hit. If the target is beyond normal range but within long range, it has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the save.

entries.name: Reach
entries: A weapon with the reach property adds 5 feet to your reach with it.

entries.name: Returning
entries: When you throw a weapon with the returning property, it automatically returns to your hand after the attack is complete, whether you hit or miss.

entries.name: {@item Slug cartridge|sw5e-phb|Slug Cartridge}
entries: Weapons with the {@item Slug cartridge|sw5e-phb|slug cartridge} property fire slug cartridges, which must be loaded in order to fire the weapon.

entries.name: Special
entries: A weapon with the special property has unusual rules governing its use, explained in the weapon's description (see "Special Weapons" later in this section).

entries.name: Specialized
entries: A weapon with the specialized property bypasses the base and cap of certain properties. Another weapon property in parentheses with the property-the weapon property that the exotic bypasses the base and cap for.

entries.name: Thrown
entries: Weapons with the thrown property can be thrown to make a ranged attack. If the weapon would normally be used to make melee weapon attacks, you use the same ability modifier for that {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} and damage roll that you would use for a melee attack with the weapon.

entries.name: Two-Handed
entries: A weapon with the two-handed property requires two hands to use.

entries.name: Versatile
entries: A weapon with the versatile property can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property—the damage when the weapon is used with two hands to make a melee attack.

entries.name: Strength
entries: A weapon with the strength property has a heavy kickback. While wielding it, you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} unless you meet the Strength requirement. If the weapon has the burst, penetrating, or rapid property, you must meet the Strength requirement to use this feature. If the weapon lacks the two-handed property, you can wield the weapon in two hands to temporarily reduce the strength number by one step (from 19 to 17, 17 to 15, 15 to 13, or 13 to 11). If this would reduce the strength number below 11, you ignore it entirely.
